title: Add NVTX ranges, runtime counters, microbench harness and perf dashboard for runtime profiling
author: Mateo Chen
description: Motivation: We need higher-fidelity runtime instrumentation to diagnose tail-latency spikes and kernel-level hotspots observed in production canaries. This PR adds NVTX ranges for key inference codepaths, exposes counters for KV-cache hits/misses and batching statistics, introduces a small microbenchmark harness to reproduce critical latencies locally, and ships an opinionated Grafana dashboard and CI microbench job. Changes are intentionally minimal and incremental: NVTX ranges are non-functional annotations; counters are lightweight atomics with opt-in collection; microbench is optional under tools/microbench and guarded by a feature flag. Checklist: - [x] Add NVTX ranges around attention, KV cache lookup, decode loop, and kernel launch points - [x] Export runtime counters via /metrics and a new perf_events endpoint (opt-in) - [x] Add microbench harness to reproduce single-request and batched throughput/latency - [x] Add Grafana dashboard JSON and example dashboard provisioning - [x] Add CI perf-workflow that runs microbench on a pinned test image and posts results to build artifact - [x] Update docs/perf/instrumentation.md and quickstart snippet for using the harness Breaking changes: none. Backwards compatibility: runtime behavior unchanged when perf collection is disabled. How to use: 1) Build with PERF_INSTRUMENTATION=1 to enable counters (NVTX no-ops if NVTX not on system). 2) Run tools/microbench/microbench.py --profile attention --batch-size 8 to collect local profiles and generated NVTX-capable tracezip. 3) Load observability/dashboards/runtime_perf.json into Grafana or use the included provisioning example. Implementation notes: - NVTX ranges added as scoped macros (NVTX_RANGE("name")) in runtime/attention and runtime/kv_cache; they compile to no-ops when NVTX support absent. - Counters implemented as atomic_u64 in runtime/metrics and exposed via existing metrics path; added an opt-in /perf_events HTTP endpoint for detailed counters when enabled. - Microbench harness is a small Python tool that can run with local model stubs or against a dev runtime; it records latency histograms, KV cache hit/miss rates, and kernel launch counts. - Dashboard contains panels for per-request token time, KV cache hit ratio, batching efficiency, kernel time breakdown (attention, matmul, softmax), and trace heatmap. - CI workflow uses a pinned CUDA base image to run microbench and upload artifacts; a simple regression check fails the job if 95th percentile latency increases by >10% compared to the recorded baseline. Security considerations: perf endpoint is opt-in and disabled by default; added RBAC note in docs. Related: ENG-4123 (runtime perf investigation), SUP-8791 (customer incident: tail spikes).

Add atomic counters for KV cache hits/misses and batching metrics
Implement microbench harness and CI perf workflow
Add Grafana dashboard JSON and provisioning example
Docs: instrumentation guide and usage examples
review_comments: Samir: Could you reduce NVTX granularity in the hot decode loop? We saw overhead in previous experiments.
Author (Mateo): NVTX is enabled only when PERF_INSTRUMENTATION=1. Granularity reduced for per-token ranges; kept per-layer and per-kernel ranges for visibility.
Jordan: The atomic counters look fine but please make sure they are cacheline padded to avoid false sharing.
Author: Added CACHELINE_PAD macro and applied to counter structs.
Priya: CI perf job failed on first run due to flaky container image pull. Can we add retry?
Author: Added retry logic and pinned image digest; re-ran CI.
merge_outcome: merged (squash and merge) after approvals from Samir, Jordan and Priya and green CI
release_notes: Added optional runtime instrumentation: NVTX ranges, lightweight counters for KV cache and batching; microbench harness and Grafana dashboard for performance debugging. No behavioral changes when disabled.
notes: This PR is focused on observability-only changes; follow-up PRs will add more NVTX ranges and link traces to request IDs. Microbench baselines are stored as CI artifacts (see perf-workflow).
